answers.question: My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?
answers.answer:
No, do not double to 80 miles or add doubles. You are 5 weeks from the start line, not 5 months, and the window for building volume has closed. The question now is sharpening and arriving fresh, not catching up to anyone else.

Jumping from 40 to 80 in one week is roughly the single biggest predictor of injury I can name. Different runners also need different mileage to run the same time, and you are already on track for sub-3:45 at your current load: easy pace 9:50/mi at 139 bpm, 20-miler done two weeks ago, 15-miler this week with low drift. We will peak around 45 to 48 miles, then taper. Trust the plan.

new.analysis:
## The week behind
You hit every planned session and the numbers back it up. Easy days sat at 139 bpm, the Wednesday workout held the goal-pace block, and Sunday's 15 at 9:59/mi with only +5.6 bpm drift says the aerobic engine is in good shape.

## Where we are
At 5 weeks out we are in the sharpest part of the build. The 20-miler two weeks ago is still in the bank, so this Sunday I want 20 again but with the last 8 at marathon pace, about 8:35/mi. That is the single most race-specific session you will do before the taper.

## Why the volume stays near 45
Your base before this block was 30 miles a week, and you are already running 40 to 53. Adding one more quality mile matters more than adding ten junk miles. Next week lands around 46 miles with the long run doing the heavy lifting, then we hold one more peak week before a two-week taper.

## On the club mate question
Comparison is the fastest way to wreck a build. Hold the line, do the work in front of you, and the under-3:45 is there.
